channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula identifica Baixada Fluminense como área prioritária no Sudeste e deve voltar duas vezes ao Rio
item.description: Lula prioritizes the Baixada Fluminense region in his campaign and plans two trips to Rio before the first round, aiming to curb the advance of right-wing figures such as Flávio Bolsonaro and Márcio Canella. The strategy includes local alliances to expand support in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Girão vê “incoerência” do PL no apoio a Ciro Gomes e elogia Michelle
item.description: Eduardo Girão criticized PL for supporting Ciro Gomes in Ceará, calling the alliance incoherent and contrary to right-wing values. He praised Michelle Bolsonaro for maintaining a position against the party, highlighting her disagreement with Flávio Bolsonaro. Girão emphasized the importance of defending life and conservative values, stating that Michelle will not support Ciro Gomes.

item.title: Jingles 2026: saiba quais mensagens os candidatos querem passar
item.description: The first 2026 presidential campaign jingles range from funk to rock and sertanejo, highlighting candidates' trajectories and proposals on security, economy, and courage to change Brazil. Lula reminisces his working-class journey and migration from the sertão, while Flávio Bolsonaro emphasizes faith, hope, and courage. Three out of four opposition jingles focus on criticisms of the current government, except Flávio's, which avoids direct attacks.

item.title: Estilo de vida de Lulinha só é acessível a 0,8% dos espanhóis
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva's lifestyle in Spain requires an annual income of approximately €208,800, a level only 0.8% of Spanish workers reach. He resides in a luxury condominium in Madrid, with monthly housing costs of around €5,800.

item.title: E os debates, hein?
item.description: A poll published by Blog Enquetes revealed that 65.3% of 818 readers viewed Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema's participation in the first presidential debate positively, while 34.7% negatively assessed other candidates' absences. The content also references political analyses on government agendas and institutional relations.

item.title: 8 de Janeiro vira trampolim eleitoral para parentes, advogados e golpistas
item.description: The 2026 election brings to the congressional race figures linked to the January 8th coup plot, such as relatives of convicts, defense lawyers and direct participants, with amnesty and criticism of the Supreme Court as banners. Right-wing presidential candidates have also adopted the theme in their campaigns, expanding the scope beyond the Bolsonaro family. Among the highlighted names are Jeffrey Chiquini, Sebastião Coelho, Carolina Siebra, Cláudia Rodrigues, Mariana Naime and Luíza Cunha, who use the defense of the accused as electoral capital.

item.title: Fim da 6x1 cria dilema fatal para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The end of the 6x1 workweek creates division in the Senate, with senators calling the measure innocuous and election-driven, warning of economic risks. Supporters highlight the benefit of extra time for workers' families. The debate reflects parliamentary tensions over labor reforms.

item.title: Tarcísio tenta manter 'distância estratégica' de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas publicly supports Flávio Bolsonaro but avoids joint events in contentious areas, focusing on controlled gatherings. Allies of the senator criticize the governor for lacking engagement in the shared campaign efforts.

item.title: Número de candidatos a governador cai; SP lidera queda e Minas vai na contramão
item.description: The average number of gubernatorial candidates in the 2026 elections dropped to 7.2 per state, compared to 8.3 in 2022 and 7.6 in 2018. São Paulo records the lowest number in its history (7 candidates), while Minas Gerais leads the increase, rising from 8 to 11 candidates. Political coordination during the pre-campaign, such as the 'scare-off' effect, directly influences the number of candidacies in each state.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja as datas do primeiro e segundo turno
item.description: The 2026 elections in Brazil will be held in two rounds: the first on October 4th, covering federal and state deputies, senators, governors, and the president. The second round, if needed, will take place on October 25th, only for the presidential and gubernatorial races where no candidate reaches over 50% of valid votes in the first round.

item.title: Nikolas Ferreira quer eleger ‘exército’ de aliados para ampliar influência política
item.description: Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) aims to build a parallel bench with candidates in every Brazilian state, strengthening his political influence in Congress and the Minas Gerais legislature. While the PL manages internal conflicts involving Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro, Ferreira focuses on creating a loyal and ideologically aligned team.

item.title: A vanguarda do atraso
item.description: The text examines Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's role in Brazilian politics, emphasizing investigations into alleged irregularities and accusations of media manipulation aimed at undermining his reelection. It underscores Lula's historical significance as a central electoral figure since 1989, comparing his legacy with other leaders and questioning Brazil's structural inequality.

item.title: Veja a agenda dos candidatos ao governo de SP nesta terça (25/8)
item.description: On Tuesday (August 25), the seven gubernatorial candidates in São Paulo carry out their campaign agendas, with emphasis on Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad. Activities include recordings, Q&A sessions, infrastructure events, and sector debates.

item.title: Perdas e ganhos
item.description: The 2026 presidential election is being shaped by decisions from the Supreme Court (STF) and the Federal Police (PF), impacting the popularity of candidates such as Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula. Three Supreme Court justices are central to rulings affecting public opinion polls. The article underscores the institutional influence on the electoral landscape.

item.title: Em Alagoas, Flávio Bolsonaro abre giro pelo Nordeste com evangélicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro kicks off his Northeast campaign leg with a stop in Alagoas, engaging evangelicals and business leaders without large rallies. However, he faces hurdles in a region where Lula holds a strong lead in voter preferences.

item.title: Diferenças entre as duas eleições
item.description: The 2026 election shows a higher rate of undecided voters (51% in the latest Quaest poll) compared to 2022 (36%), with Lula's supporters showing greater electoral interest. The campaign started colder, but Lula retains strong support in the Northeast region.

item.title: 'A política virou um manicômio', diz Augusto Cury após estreia em debates
item.description: Augusto Cury, Avante's presidential candidate, criticized political polarization and a toxic environment, highlighting his low poll numbers (2%) and debate struggles. He condemned the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, recited self-help phrases from his books, and claimed to be the only one capable of uniting the nation.

item.title: Lula mobiliza movimentos sociais para campanha de rua e mira indecisos
item.description: Lula mobilizes social movements for street campaigns, using initiatives like 'Sextou com Lula' and propaganda brigades to engage the base and win over undecided voters. The strategy employs festivals, music, and leafleting in 60 cities to discuss proposals and attract young people.

item.title: As eleições desse ano são para quais cargos?
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections decide five positions: federal deputy, state deputy, senator, governor, and president. The first round takes place on October 4, with a potential second round on October 25.

item.title: A mudança de humor de Lula após as investigações envolvendo seu filho
item.description: Lula, initially calm and confident, showed greater concern and worry about his 2026 reelection campaign after investigations involved his son. This mood shift reflects the potential electoral impact of ongoing legal cases.

item.title: O plano do STJ para a denúncia contra Zema por vídeo de fantoche de Gilmar Mendes
item.description: The Superior Court of Justice (STJ) postponed the analysis of the lawsuit against Romeu Zema regarding a satirical video featuring Supreme Federal Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, deferring the case until after the elections. The Federal Prosecution Service accuses Zema of slander if the video is deemed offensive to the magistrate. The matter highlights judicial polarization involving the Novo Party's presidential candidate.

item.title: Governo Lula debate regulamentar acesso a dados e transparência de anúncios de big techs
item.description: The Lula administration is considering regulating big techs' data access and ad transparency, requiring platforms to disclose how they provide data on sold ads and promotions. The measure aims to enhance oversight and clarity of digital advertising practices.

item.title: Ancine concede registro a “Dark Horse”, filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Ancine granted the Foreign Work Registry to 'Dark Horse', a biographical film about Jair Bolsonaro, which has been mired in controversy over alleged misuse of funds tied to its financing and connections to the Bolsonaro family. A federal investigation, heard at the STF, scrutinizes the origin and destination of R$ 61 million funneled into a fund linked to Eduardo Bolsonaro’s lawyer. The case prompted Ancine to open an administrative process against Go Up Entertainment.

item.title: Jair Bolsonaro não poderá votar nas eleições, mas presos provisórios, sim; entenda
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro, sentenced to over 27 years for involvement in the coup plot, had his political rights suspended and cannot vote in the 2026 elections. In contrast, provisional detainees retain voting rights, per a TSE ruling. The case also affects other Bolsonaro family members, with Flávio and Michelle running under judicial restrictions.

item.title: Evangelização no YouTube, autoajuda para casal e emenda para recapear condomínio: quem é o deputado mais seguido do país
item.description: Federal deputy Fábio Teruel (MDB-SP), with 44.2 million followers, is the most followed politician in Brazil after former president Jair Bolsonaro. He entered politics in 2022 after building a large audience on YouTube with content focused on evangelization and self-help. Despite his massive followership, Teruel claims his political influence primarily comes from radio and WhatsApp groups, keeping social media for religious purposes.

item.title: Campanha de Lula prepara ato com pedetista no Rio Grande do Sul e evento para mulheres em Minas
item.description: Lula kicks off his reelection campaign with events in Rio Grande do Sul and Minas, aligning with pedetista Juliana Brizola and emphasizing a female-focused strategy against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Decisão de Dino sobre compartilhamento de dados de 'Dark Horse' à PF amplia pressão no STF sobre investigações
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino authorized Federal Police access to data seized by São Paulo Civil Police in an investigation into the financing of the film 'Dark Horse', increasing pressure on the Supreme Court. The decision enables cross-referencing between two parallel investigations: one regarding alleged misuse of parliamentary amendments, led by Dino, and another concerning the origin of funds from former banker Daniel Vorcaro, led by André Mendonça. Both probes involve the production company Go Up Entertainment and former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Menos pastel, mais nicho: Tarcísio prioriza militância, agro e empresários a agendas de rua na largada da campanha
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas launched his re-election campaign focusing on niche audiences like agribusiness, business leaders, and religious groups, avoiding street events and relying on social media communication. He leads polls with 45% voting intentions, followed by Fernando Haddad with 27%. The campaign plans to intensify street actions from September, focusing on Greater São Paulo.

item.title: Lula evita estados em que mais de um candidato disputam seu apoio para reduzir atritos na campanha à reeleição
item.description: Lula avoids visiting states like Pernambuco, Paraíba, and Maranhão, where multiple candidates compete for his endorsement, to minimize internal conflicts in the reelection campaign. In Pernambuco, João Campos (PSB) and Raquel Lyra (PSD) both seek Lula's support, leading to a balanced strategy between local alliances and the national ticket for 2026.

item.title: De acenos ao bolsonarismo a 'herança maldita': entenda em seis pontos como foi a entrevista de Zema à TV Globo
item.description: Zema courted the right by criticizing the STF and supporting vaccination but avoided direct attacks on Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. He emphasized a 'cursed legacy' from predecessors and advocated for conditional amnesty for January 8th coup plotters.

item.title: O GLOBO, Valor e CBN sabatinam Romeu Zema com transmissão ao vivo e abrem série de entrevistas com presidenciáveis
item.description: O GLOBO, Valor and CBN will hold live interviews with 2026 presidential candidates, starting with Romeu Zema (Novo) at 10:30 AM, followed by Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro were invited but have not confirmed. Interviews take place at the GLOBO studio in Rio with live broadcast and media coverage.

item.title: 'Aumentar dez vezes': Zema promete levar ensino integral ao quádruplo de escolas que existem no país
item.description: Candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) promised to increase by tenfold the number of schools with full-time education in Brazil, raising the target from 49,900 to 499,000 institutions. Despite the ambition of the proposal, the total number of public schools in the country is 137,000, making the goal challenging. Zema highlighted the progress in Minas Gerais, where he multiplied by 12 the number of schools with full-time education.

item.title: 'BolsoPaes': família Reis puxa dobradinha que une voto no ex-prefeito e em Flávio na Baixada
item.description: The Reis family, a key political force in Duque de Caxias, supports both Eduardo Paes (PSD) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tickets, creating a complex alliance mixing support for PT and PL. Jane Reis, running for vice-governor on Paes' ticket, leads the effort while MDB and PSD candidates use campaign materials referencing Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lobista pagou em dinheiro passagens de Lulinha, diz PF
item.description: Messages seized by the Federal Police suggest that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger managed the finances of Fábio Luís da Silva, son of President Lula, and paid for his flights. The investigation also hints at commercial operations and money laundering, including a suspected R$300,000 payment to Lulinha from the "Careca do INSS." While Lulinha's defense denies wrongdoing, the case feeds into broader corruption and money laundering probes.

item.title: Duas Linhas e Meia (25-08-2026)
item.description: Renata Almeida Magalhães, president of the Brazilian Academy of Cinema and prominent audiovisual producer, will be honored on August 17th at Estação Gávea with the Pedro Ernesto Merit Medals. The ceremony recognizes her career in cinema, which began at age 17 with the short film 'Vitória' (1979).

item.title: Deputado goiano é investigado por usar empresas fantasmas no Entorno
item.description: Goias state deputy Andre do Premium (Brazilian Union-GO) is under investigation for allegedly using shell companies to hide assets and evade tax debts of R$24.6 million. The companies Premium Comercio de Alimentos and Atacadao Premium would have been transferred to frontmen without financial capacity, using inadequate addresses such as vacant lots and public agencies.

item.title: Após primeira semana de exibição, 'Por você' registra aumento na média de audiência em relação a antecessora
item.description: The telenovela 'Por você', starring Sheron Menezzes, leads viewership in its first week, outperforming its predecessor 'Coração acelerado'. In São Paulo, the show achieved 20 points, a two-point increase compared to the previous average.

item.title: Lulinha disse a lobista que viagem em grupo à Europa era “arriscada”
item.description: Federal Police messages reveal that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, opposed a group trip to Europe organized by a lobbyist, citing risks and suggesting postponement. Investigations indicate destinations such as Switzerland and Liechtenstein, with purposes including bank account openings and potential financial obfuscation.

item.title: Carta abierta de Sergio Ramírez al presidente Lula da Silva
item.description: Sergio Ramírez writes an open letter to President Lula da Silva, recalling their meeting in 1991 during the first Sandinista Front congress in Managua. Ramírez emphasizes the importance of electoral democracy and criticizes Daniel Ortega's dictatorship in Nicaragua, expressing support for Brazil's democratic system and respect for electoral results.

item.title: 'Taxa das blusinhas', fim da 6x1, terras raras: Lula tenta destravar pautas do governo em reunião com Alcolumbre e Motta
item.description: Lula meets with Alcolumbre and Motta to discuss approving agendas including end of 6x1 scale, public security, rare earths and review of fees on low-value imports.

item.title: STF faz audiência pública sobre combate a facções criminosas; Lei Antifacção é questionada na Corte
item.description: The STF holds a public hearing to debate the constitutionality of the Anti-Gang Law, which faces four lawsuits filed by legal associations and the Public Ministry. Justices advocate for inter-institutional cooperation to combat organized crime in a coordinated manner, criticizing the current fragmented approach to public security. The law was signed by President Lula in March this year.

item.title: Deepfake nas eleições: entenda o que é e por que pode enganar o eleitor
item.description: Deepfakes are manipulated images or audio created using AI that can mislead voters, spreading false content and eroding trust in real media. The TSE banned their use in electoral campaigns starting in 2024, imposing strict restrictions during election periods. Sharing deepfakes may lead to legal consequences if intentional misinformation or fraud is proven.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Relator descarta mudanças e diz que trabalha para votar texto em comissão do Senado na próxima semana
item.description: The rapporteur of the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule in the Senate, Senator Omar Aziz, stated he will not make changes to the text and plans to vote the report at the CCJ next week, advancing to plenary consideration between August 31 and September 4. The proposal reduces the weekly work hours from 44 to 42 in two months, without salary cuts. Lula pressures for approval before the October municipal elections.

item.title: Flávio desembarca em Alagoas para estreia no Nordeste com ausências esperadas de JHC e Lira
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro kicks off his presidential campaign in the Northeast with a stop in Alagoas, but faces challenges without the backing of JHC and Arthur Lira. Despite being the running mate in Alagoas, the senator arrives in the state without uniting key local figures, reflecting difficulties in building alliances where Lula leads significantly.

item.title: Propostas de presidenciáveis priorizam reação à prevenção da violência contra crianças, diz Unicef
item.description: The Unicef analyzed the government plans of the five main 2026 presidential candidates and found that, while proposals against violence toward children and adolescents exist, most prioritize punitive responses (such as increased penalties and policing) over preventive actions. Candidates like Lula and Caiado focus on combating violence, whereas Zema, Bolsonaro, and Renan emphasize education. The report underscores the need for preventive social policies to effectively protect children and adolescents.

item.title: Erika desafia Flávio para debate sobre 6x1: “Vai aceitar ou passar mal?”
item.description: Federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSol-SP) challenged Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) to a public debate on the PEC proposing the end of the 6×1 work schedule. The invitation was made on social media after a O Globo report indicated that Flávio's allies are trying to block the PEC in Congress.

item.title: Como foi o debate da Band: Caiado, Renan e Cury disparam ataques contra Lula e Flávio; veja repercussão
item.description: In the first presidential debate on Band, Caiado, Renan and Cury attacked Lula and Flávio, while the event was the emptiest since 1989. Lula gave an interview to Record and Flávio released an alternative video. The main debates focused on economy, security and corruption.

item.title: Coordenador de campanha de Lula defende recompra de títulos da dívida e alta de imposto para super-ricos
item.description: José Sergio Gabrielli, Lula's (PT) campaign coordinator, advocates for government intervention in public debt markets to lower long-term interest rates and suggests higher taxes for the wealthy. These measures aim to stabilize the economy and promote wealth redistribution.

item.title: O que Romeu Zema disse em sabatina do Jornal Nacional com presidenciáveis
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate from the New Party, participated in a Jornal Nacional town hall, promising to privatize state-owned companies, classify criminal factions as terrorist organizations, and grant amnesty to those convicted in connection with the January 8, 2023 events. The interview was the first of six scheduled with presidential candidates this week.

item.title: Zema diz que tribunais fazem “mais política do que justiça”
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) stated in an interview with Jornal Nacional that Brazilian courts are acting with political bias, particularly in STF judgments regarding the January 8th events and Jair Bolsonaro's conviction. He advocated for pardoning the defendants and questioned whether the incidents constituted a coup attempt, calling the convictions a 'clearly political trial.' Despite his remarks, he emphasized trust in electronic voting and commitment to democracy.
